question: Which type of vehicle is commonly used in zero-emission public transport systems?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric buses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Electric buses are a crucial component of zero-emission public transport systems as they run on electricity rather than fossil fuels, reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• These buses typically use rechargeable batteries or are powered by electricity supplied through overhead lines, making them environmentally friendly.
 
• Many cities globally have adopted electric buses to combat air pollution and to meet climate change mitigation targets.
 
• Electric buses contribute to improved urban air quality by eliminating tailpipe emissions, including carbon dioxide (CO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx), and particulate matter.
 
• Governments and transport authorities often incentivize the adoption of electric buses through subsidies, tax exemptions, and infrastructure development for charging stations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs)**:

 
 
• These are vehicles that produce no tailpipe emissions, including electric vehicles (EVs) and hydrogen fuel cell vehicles.
 
• They play a significant role in reducing air pollution and combating climate change.
 
 
 
• **Battery technology in electric buses**:
 
 
• Electric buses often use lithium-ion batteries due to their high energy density, long lifespan, and rapid charging capabilities.
 
• Advances in battery technology have improved the range and efficiency of modern electric buses.
 
 
 
• **Economic benefits of electric buses**:
 
 
• Electric buses have lower operational and maintenance costs compared to diesel-powered buses.
 
• They reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels, contributing to energy security.
 
 
 
• **Global adoption of electric buses**:
 
 
• Cities like Shenzhen (China) have fully transitioned to electric buses, showcasing their feasibility on a large scale.
 
• India, under schemes such as FAME (Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles), is promoting electric buses in urban transport systems.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in electric bus implementation**:
 
 
• High upfront costs for purchasing electric buses and establishing charging infrastructure.
 
• Limited range compared to traditional diesel buses, though ongoing technological advancements are addressing this issue.
